reuse.why: Most consumers reuse getScheduleAmount, but the API independently calculates expected amounts and the helper repeats the existing getApproxNumberThreshold formula.

duplication.why: The diff introduces a separate schedule-amount decision in the API and duplicates the shared approximate-tolerance calculation.

placement.why: The shared schedules module is appropriate for amount policy, but scheduleModel.toExternal embeds a competing domain decision in the serialization layer.

scope.why: The edits remain focused on expected schedule amounts, their consumers, API types, and associated tests.

maintainability.why: Independent API amount logic and a copied tolerance formula leave maintainers multiple definitions to reconcile when the policy changes.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/api-models.ts: scheduleModel.toExternal bypasses getScheduleAmount; packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts: getScheduleAmount bypasses getApproxNumberThreshold.

disguised_duplication.where: scheduleModel.toExternal reshapes the shared amount decision into a local numeric/range ternary and absolute-value endpoint comparison instead of delegating to getScheduleAmount.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduleAmount gains the optional op parameter and an isapprox branch, while scheduleModel.toExternal independently implements the amount decision and remains outside subsequent shared policy changes.
